section_summary: This section covers United States and Allied policy formulation, internal Japanese developments, and public commentary concerning the reform, demilitarization, and reorganization of Japan's educational system following World War II. It includes reports from the U.S. Political Adviser in Tokyo on Japanese student and teacher union activities, curricula revisions, and extensive educational reform proposals submitted by Watanabe Chugo. Additionally, the records document diplomatic exchanges with Australia, inter-agency deliberations within the State-War-Navy Coordinating Committee (SWNCC) regarding departmental responsibility and budgeting, advocacy by the Committee on Women in World Affairs to include female educators on the U.S. educational mission, and inquiries regarding textbook censorship and religious policy.

subfiles.about: This document contains the concluding portion of a memorandum reporting on Japanese teacher unionization, university curricula changes, faculty reinstatements, and plans for a women's university.
subfiles.from: Dr. K. C. Leebrick
subfiles.summary: Concluding pages of a memorandum detailing the Japanese Educationalists Union platform, university curriculum and faculty changes, and plans for a women's university in Nagoya.
subfiles.title: Educational Affairs in Japan, November 9 to December 1, 1945 (Concluding Pages)
subfiles.to: Office of the United States Political Adviser, Tokyo

subfiles.about: This cover despatch transmits Dr. K. C. Leebrick's memorandum on educational affairs in Japan from November 9 to December 1, 1945.
subfiles.from: George Atcheson, Jr., Acting United States Political Adviser, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Transmits Dr. K. C. Leebrick's memorandum reviewing educational developments and reform progress in Japan.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 90: Educational Affairs in Japan, November 9 to December 1, 1945
subfiles.to: The Secretary of State, Washington

subfiles.about: This memorandum surveys official educational actions, student activism, teacher organization, university curriculum revisions, and faculty changes across Japan during late 1945.
subfiles.from: Dr. K. C. Leebrick
subfiles.summary: This memorandum surveys significant educational developments in Japan between November 9 and December 1, 1945. It details Ministry of Education ordinances promoting social and scientific education, the prohibition of military training, school reconstruction, and principal reshuffles. Furthermore, it analyzes student unrest, the establishment of the Japanese Educationalists Union, curricula and faculty reinstatements across imperial universities, and plans for a women's university in Nagoya.
subfiles.title: Memorandum: Educational Affairs in Japan, November 9 to December 1, 1945
subfiles.to: Office of the United States Political Adviser, Tokyo

subfiles.about: This memorandum records a telephone discussion with Alan S. Watt regarding Australian interest in exchanging ideas on Japanese re-education plans.
subfiles.from: Hugh Borton, Division of Japanese Affairs
subfiles.summary: Records preliminary arrangements with Alan S. Watt for informal discussions regarding Japanese re-education planning.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation: Interest of Australian Government in Formulation of a Comprehensive and Coordinated Plan of Reeducation in Japan
subfiles.to: Department of State

subfiles.about: This memorandum details an informal exchange of views between Australian representative W. D. Forsyth and State Department officers on Japanese educational reform policies.
subfiles.from: Hugh Borton, Division of Japanese Affairs
subfiles.summary: Details discussions with W. D. Forsyth on Australian perspectives regarding Japanese re-education, emphasizing women's education, imperial rescript reform, and Nisei involvement.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation: Interest of Australian Government in Formulation of a Plan of Reeducation in Japan
subfiles.to: Department of State

subfiles.about: This memorandum attaches the final draft of the SWNCC paper on State Department responsibility for Japanese reorientation prior to Joint Chiefs of Staff review.
subfiles.from: William T. Stone, Director, Office of International Information and Cultural Affairs
subfiles.summary: Reports on SWNCC subcommittee approval of the Japanese reorientation policy paper and its transmittal to the Joint Chiefs.
subfiles.title: Memorandum: Final Draft of SWNCC Paper on Reorientation of the Japanese
subfiles.to: William Benton, Assistant Secretary of State

subfiles.about: This memorandum announces the full SWNCC approval of SWNCC 162/4 placing basic planning responsibility for Japanese reorientation on the State Department.
subfiles.from: William T. Stone, Director, Office of International Information and Cultural Affairs
subfiles.summary: Reports SWNCC approval of SWNCC 162/4 assigning Japanese reorientation planning to State and notes necessary budget increases.
subfiles.title: Memorandum: Approval of SWNCC 162/4, 'Reorientation of the Japanese'
subfiles.to: William Benton, Assistant Secretary of State

subfiles.about: This memorandum outlines staffing needs, budget negotiations with the Bureau of the Budget, and plans for an advisory committee on Japanese re-education.
subfiles.from: William T. Stone, Director, Office of International Information and Cultural Affairs
subfiles.summary: Summarizes discussions with the Bureau of the Budget concerning inadequate staffing and proposes appointing an advisory committee on long-term re-education.
subfiles.title: Office Memorandum: Department's Responsibility for Re-education Policy in Japan
subfiles.to: William Benton, Assistant Secretary of State

subfiles.about: This diplomatic note conveys the Australian Government's desire to participate in formulating comprehensive re-education directives for Japan.
subfiles.from: Sir Frederic Eggleston, Australian Minister to the United States
subfiles.summary: Expresses Australia's desire to consult on and participate in formulating the master plan for Japanese re-education.
subfiles.title: Australian Legation Note No. 425/45 on Japanese Re-education Plan
subfiles.to: Dean Acheson, Acting Secretary of State

subfiles.about: This memorandum reports that the Australian Legation requested advance drafts of Japanese re-education plans at the working level.
subfiles.from: George H. Blakeslee, Office of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: Reports Sir Frederic Eggleston's request to review working-level American drafts concerning Japanese reorientation and re-education.
subfiles.title: Memorandum: Australian Participation in Japanese Re-education Plans
subfiles.to: John Carter Vincent, Director, Office of Far Eastern Affairs

subfiles.about: This memorandum transmits Sir George Sansom's thoughts on Japanese re-education for consideration in basic policy drafting.
subfiles.from: Archibald MacLeish, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Asks whether Sir George Sansom's views on Japanese re-education should be considered when drafting basic policy papers.
subfiles.title: Memorandum: Sir George Sansom's Views on Japanese Re-education
subfiles.to: John Sloan Dickey, Director, Office of Public Information

subfiles.about: This memorandum designates Gordon T. Bowles to represent the Division of Cultural Cooperation and MacLeish's office regarding Japanese re-education.
subfiles.from: Archibald MacLeish, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Designates Gordon T. Bowles to handle Japanese re-education policy coordination for the Division of Cultural Cooperation.
subfiles.title: Memorandum: Representation of Division of Cultural Cooperation on Japanese Re-education
subfiles.to: Bryn J. Hovde, Chief, Division of Cultural Cooperation, and Eugene H. Dooman, Special Assistant

subfiles.about: This letter clarifies that Allied Council Chairman Sebald did not make statements regarding decentralization reported by the New York Times.
subfiles.from: Frank A. Schuler, Jr., Chief, Japanese-Korean Branch, Division of Occupied Areas
subfiles.summary: Clarifies that remarks on Japanese educational decentralization were made by Patrick Shaw, not William J. Sebald.
subfiles.title: Letter to Professor Robert King Hall Regarding Educational Decentralization
subfiles.to: Professor Robert King Hall, Teachers College, Columbia University

subfiles.about: This letter expresses concern over reports that an Allied board of chaplains was established to review religious content in Japanese textbooks.
subfiles.from: Professor Robert King Hall, Teachers College, Columbia University
subfiles.summary: Questions the establishment of an Allied chaplains board to review Japanese school textbooks, warning it violates religious freedom.
subfiles.title: Letter from Professor Robert King Hall Concerning Board of Chaplains Reviewing Textbooks
subfiles.to: Frank A. Schuler, Jr., Chief, Japanese-Korean Branch, Division of Occupied Areas

subfiles.about: This letter extract explains corrective action taken regarding errors in a history textbook and describes the role of the Board of Chaplains.
subfiles.from: General Douglas MacArthur, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.summary: Explains corrections made to a Japanese textbook and clarifies the Board of Chaplains' role in reviewing Christian content.
subfiles.title: Letter from General Douglas MacArthur Concerning Errors in Textbook 'History of the West' and Board of Chaplains
subfiles.to: Unidentified recipient

subfiles.about: This letter urges the appointment of additional women educators to the advisory mission assisting with Japan's educational reform.
subfiles.from: Dr. Emily Hickman, Chairman, Committee on Women in World Affairs
keywords: Committee on Women in World Affairs
subfiles.summary: Urges the appointment of more women educators to the advisory group assisting in reforming Japan's educational system.
subfiles.title: Letter from Committee on Women in World Affairs to Secretary of State Byrnes
subfiles.to: James F. Byrnes, Secretary of State

subfiles.about: This letter petitions President Truman to include qualified female educators in the advisory mission on the Japanese educational system.
subfiles.from: Dr. Emily Hickman, Chairman, Committee on Women in World Affairs
keywords: Committee on Women in World Affairs
subfiles.summary: Petitions President Truman to appoint additional qualified women to the United States educational advisory group for Japan.
subfiles.title: Letter from Committee on Women in World Affairs to President Truman
subfiles.to: Harry S. Truman, President of the United States

subfiles.about: This routing slip forwards correspondence regarding the inclusion of women educators in the educational mission to Japan.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 270: Transmission of Two Statements by WATANABE Chugo on Educational Reform
subfiles.to: The Secretary of State, Washington

subfiles.about: This memorandum outlines substantial educational reforms, a proposed school system, and key objectives for democratizing education in Japan.
subfiles.from: Chugo Watanabe, former Director of Japan Trade Promotion Association
subfiles.summary: This memorandum outlines substantial reforms aimed at eliminating militarism, ultra-nationalism, and academic cliquism from Japanese education. It proposes replacing national schools with an eight-year co-educational compulsory public school system, establishing three-year middle schools, adopting a university quarter system, and transferring state universities to prefectures. Furthermore, it advocates abolishing entrance examinations, restructuring teacher training, and modernizing language and English instruction.
subfiles.title: Memorandum: Gist of Proposed Reform of Education
subfiles.to: Office of the United States Political Adviser, Tokyo

subfiles.about: This detailed proposal elaborates on dismantling imperial universities, reorganizing schools, establishing local university clusters, and eradicating corrupt administrative practices.
subfiles.from: Chugo Watanabe, former Director of Japan Trade Promotion Association
subfiles.summary: This detailed plan proposes concrete measures to break up the bureaucratic monopoly of imperial universities, disperse higher educational institutions to prefectures, and consolidate Tokyo colleges into regional universities. It calls for ending corrupt practices such as the school inspector and book recommendation systems, introducing school committees with guardian and teacher representation, and instituting labor discipline during summer quarters. Additionally, it urges pragmatic curriculum adjustments, Romanization, and cultural counter-measures against militaristic literature and journalism.
subfiles.title: Memorandum: Practical Application of the Educational Reform Plan
subfiles.to: Office of the United States Political Adviser, Tokyo

subfiles.about: This memorandum routes Chugo Watanabe's educational proposals to Gordon Bowles, commending the concept of establishing provincial universities.

subfiles.summary: Commends Watanabe's proposal to establish universities in the provinces outside Tokyo and routes it to Gordon Bowles.
subfiles.title: Memorandum: Comment on Watanabe's Educational Reform Proposals
